overview: Two broad categories of mutation distinguished by scale — one shifts the entire downstream reading frame, the other alters a single base.
genZNote: Point mutation: one typo. Frameshift: the whole sentence gets scrambled from that point on.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: An insertion or deletion of a number of nucleotides not divisible by three, shifting the reading frame downstream of the mutation.
aspects.valueB: A change to a single nucleotide base pair in the DNA sequence (substitution, or in a broader sense, a single-base insertion/deletion).

aspects.label: Effect on Reading Frame
aspects.valueA: Shifts the entire downstream codon reading frame, typically scrambling all subsequent amino acids and often creating a premature stop.
aspects.valueB: Does not shift the reading frame if it is a substitution — only the single affected codon may change.

aspects.label: Typical Cause
aspects.valueA: Insertion or deletion (indel) of 1, 2, 4, or 5 (non-multiple-of-3) nucleotides.
aspects.valueB: Base substitution (transition or transversion) at a single position.

aspects.label: Typical Severity
aspects.valueA: Usually severe — nearly always disrupts protein function due to a completely altered downstream sequence.
aspects.valueB: Severity varies widely — can be silent, missense, or nonsense depending on which base and codon are affected.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: A single nucleotide deletion in the CFTR gene shifting the frame and truncating the protein.
aspects.valueB: A single A-to-T substitution changing one codon, as in the sickle cell mutation.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Shifts the entire downstream reading frame; usually caused by non-multiple-of-3 indels.
aspects.valueB: Affects a single base pair; reading frame preserved if it's a substitution.
